## Description

The bucket merge processor (`bucketmergeprocessor`) reduces the number of buckets
in histogram metrics by merging adjacent buckets. It handles both histogram
representations, each with its own independent limit:

* **Classic** (explicit-bounds) histograms — interior boundaries are removed and
  the counts on either side are summed.
* **Exponential** histograms — the scale is lowered, which merges adjacent
  buckets pairwise ("downscaling").

Reducing bucket counts lowers the storage cardinality of histograms in the
backend (for example, one Prometheus/Mimir series is stored per classic bucket),
at the cost of resolution. Merging is lossless with respect to the *aggregate*
histogram: total `Count`, `Sum`, `Min` and `Max` are always preserved — only the
granularity of the distribution is reduced.

Only histogram data points whose type has a configured section are modified.
Every other metric — and every histogram type left unconfigured — passes through
unchanged. Non-histogram metrics are never touched.

## Configuration

Both sections are optional. Omitting a section passes that histogram type
through unchanged, so a configuration only needs to declare the type(s) it wants
to reduce.

```yaml
processors:
  bucketmerge:
    # Reduce classic (explicit-bounds) histograms. Omit to pass them through.
    classic:
      # Maximum number of bucket counts retained per data point, including the
      # final implicit +Inf overflow bucket. Data points already at or below
      # this many buckets are left unchanged. Must be >= 2.
      max_buckets: 10
      # How the surviving boundaries are chosen: "count", "linear" or
      # "logarithmic". See "Classic histograms" below.
      [ strategy: <string> | default = logarithmic ]
      # Which end keeps finer resolution on an uneven split: "lower" or "upper".
      [ bias: <string> | default = upper ]
      # Boundary values that must survive the merge if present in the input
      # (e.g. SLA thresholds). Take priority over max_buckets.
      [ retain_bounds: [<float>, ...] | default = [] ]

    # Reduce exponential histograms. Omit to pass them through.
    exponential:
      # Maximum number of populated buckets retained per sign (positive and
      # negative). The scale is lowered — merging adjacent buckets — until the
      # populated span fits within this limit. Must be >= 2.
      max_buckets: 20
```

### Classic histograms

`max_buckets` counts bucket *slots*, i.e. the length of `BucketCounts`, which
for a classic histogram is always one more than the number of explicit bounds
(the extra slot is the `+Inf` overflow bucket). Merging can only ever *drop*
existing boundaries and sum the counts on either side — it can never invent a new
boundary — so every strategy is a rule for choosing which of the original bounds
to keep (`max_buckets - 1` of them).

#### `strategy`

| Strategy | Equalizes across surviving buckets | Looks at |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `count` | the number of original buckets folded in | nothing (positional) |
| `linear` | bucket **width** (even spacing on a linear axis) | bound values |
| `logarithmic` (default) | bucket **ratio** (even spacing on a log axis) | bound values |

`logarithmic` suits latency and size histograms, whose bounds are usually already
roughly geometric. It requires all bounds to be positive; if any bound is `<= 0`
it falls back to `linear` for that data point (log spacing is undefined there).

All three strategies are **stable**: the surviving bounds depend only on the
input bounds, not on the observed counts, so every data point sharing a bound
layout is reduced to the same layout. This keeps the `le` set consistent across
data points and series, which downstream aggregation (e.g. `histogram_quantile`)
relies on.

#### `bias`

When the buckets do not divide evenly and one end must absorb the leftover,
`bias` decides which end keeps finer resolution: `upper` (the default — larger
groups at the low end, finer resolution at the tail) or `lower` (finer at the low
end). For example, reducing 10 buckets to 4 with `count` yields group sizes
`3,3,2,2` under `upper` and `2,2,3,3` under `lower`.

#### `retain_bounds`

Boundary values listed here always survive the merge if they are present in the
input — useful for pinning SLA/SLO thresholds (e.g. `[10, 30, 60]`). Pins take
priority over the strategy: the remaining budget is filled by the strategy, and
if the pins alone exceed `max_buckets` they are all kept and `max_buckets` is
treated as best-effort. A value that is not an exact existing bound is ignored
(the processor cannot create a boundary that was never emitted).

The `+Inf` overflow bucket is always preserved.

### Exponential histograms

Exponential histograms are reduced by lowering their `scale`. Each unit decrease
in scale merges every adjacent pair of buckets, halving the resolution — a
lossless "perfect subsetting" operation guaranteed by the exponential bucketing
scheme. The processor lowers the scale until neither the positive nor the
negative populated span (the distance between the first and last non-zero bucket)
exceeds `max_buckets`, or the minimum scale (`-10`) is reached. The positive and
negative ranges share a single scale, so they are always downscaled together.

## Examples

Reduce only exponential histograms:

```yaml
processors:
  bucketmerge:
    exponential:
      max_buckets: 40
```

Reduce both, with tighter limits on classic histograms:

```yaml
processors:
  bucketmerge:
    classic:
      max_buckets: 16
    exponential:
      max_buckets: 40
```

Keep SLA thresholds while aggressively collapsing everything else. Here the merge
is guaranteed to preserve the `1s`, `3s` and `10s` boundaries:

```yaml
processors:
  bucketmerge:
    classic:
      max_buckets: 6
      strategy: logarithmic
      retain_bounds: [1, 3, 10]
```

> Different metrics that need different limits or strategies can each be routed
> through their own `bucketmerge` instance using the [routing connector] or
> separate pipelines; the processor itself applies one configuration to every
> histogram it sees.

[routing connector]: https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/tree/main/connector/routingconnector
